questions.stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of heat?

explain.why: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat.
Wood is a poor conductor of heat.
Rubber is a poor conductor of heat.

solution: Metals such as steel are good conductors of heat.

questions.stem: Why are cooking pots usually made of metal?
options: Metal does not gain any heat from the stove
Metal is a good insulator of heat
Metal is a good conductor, so food heats quickly
Metal is a poor conductor, so heat stays inside the pot

explain.why: Metal gains heat from the stove quickly.
A good insulator is a poor conductor. Metal conducts heat well.
Metal is a good conductor of heat.

solution: A metal pot conducts heat from the stove to the food.

questions.stem: The handle of a pot is made of plastic. Why?
options: Plastic is a good conductor, so it spreads heat to the food
Plastic expands more than metal does
Plastic is a poor conductor, so the handle stays cooler
Plastic is a good conductor, so heat leaves the handle quickly

explain.why: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat.
This is not the reason a handle is made of plastic.
Plastic is a poor conductor of heat.

solution: A poor conductor does not carry the heat to our hand.

questions.stem: What usually happens to a solid when it gains heat?
options: It always turns into a gas

explain.why: Many solids expand without melting.
Most solids do not change into a gas when heated.
A solid usually contracts when it loses heat.

solution: Most solids expand when they gain heat.

questions.stem: A sealed balloon filled with air is left in the hot Sun. What happens to the air inside?

explain.why: Warm air does not turn into a liquid.
Heating does not change the mass of the air.
Air contracts when it loses heat.

solution: A gas expands when it gains heat.

questions.stem: A metal lid is stuck tightly on a glass jar. Which of these will help loosen the lid?
options: Running cold water over the lid
Putting the whole jar into a freezer
Pouring cold milk into the jar
Running hot water over the lid

explain.why: Cold makes the lid contract and grip even more tightly.
Cold makes the lid contract and grip more tightly.
This does not make the lid any bigger.

solution: Heat makes the metal lid expand, so it becomes looser.

questions.stem: There are small gaps between the sections of a railway track. Why?
options: So that the trains can travel faster
So that the tracks have space to expand on hot days
So that rain can flow away
So that the tracks can contract more on hot days

explain.why: The gaps are not there to make trains faster.
The gaps are for expansion, not drainage.
Tracks expand, not contract, on hot days.

solution: The tracks expand in the heat, and the gaps stop them from bending.

questions.stem: A thermometer is placed in hot water. What happens to the liquid inside it?
options: It stays at the same level
It expands and rises up the tube
It turns into a gas and escapes
It contracts and goes down the tube

explain.why: The liquid gains heat, so it changes.
The liquid stays inside the tube.
The liquid contracts only when it loses heat.

solution: The liquid gains heat and expands, so it rises.

questions.stem: A thermometer is moved from warm water into ice water. What happens to the liquid inside it?
options: It stays at the same level
It expands and goes up the tube

explain.why: The liquid used in a thermometer does not freeze in ice water.
The liquid loses heat, so it changes.
The liquid expands only when it gains heat.

solution: The liquid loses heat and contracts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a poor conductor of heat?

explain.why: Iron is a metal, so it is a good conductor.
Copper is a metal, so it is a good conductor.
Steel is a metal, so it is a good conductor.

solution: Wood is a poor conductor of heat.

questions.stem: Why do people wear woollen clothes in cold places?
options: Wool makes heat for the body
Trapped air in wool slows down heat loss
Wool lets the cold air go into the body
Wool is a good conductor, so it brings heat to the body

explain.why: Wool does not make heat.
Cold does not flow in. Heat flows out of the body.
Wool is a poor conductor.

solution: Trapped air slows down the heat lost from the body.

questions.stem: What happens when ice gains heat at room temperature?

explain.why: Gaining heat makes it warmer, not colder.
Condensation is a gas changing into a liquid.
Freezing happens when water loses heat.

solution: Ice melts when it gains heat.

questions.stem: What happens to water when it loses a lot of heat in a freezer?

explain.why: Boiling happens when water gains heat.
Evaporation happens when water gains heat.
Water turns into a gas when it gains heat.

solution: Water freezes when it loses enough heat.

questions.stem: A metal ball can only just pass through a ring when both are cold. The ball is heated and then placed on the ring as shown. The ball does not pass through. Why?

explain.why: The ring has not changed in mass.
Heating does not make the ball lighter.
Heat makes a solid expand.

solution: The ball gained heat and expanded, so it is too big for the ring.

questions.stem: A metal ball is just too big to pass through a ring. The ball is then cooled for a long time. What happens when it is put on the ring again?
options: It becomes too big for the ring
It still cannot pass through the ring
It melts and sticks to the ring

explain.why: Cooling makes the ball smaller, not bigger.
Cooling makes the ball contract.
Cooling does not melt a metal.

solution: The cooled ball contracts, so it is small enough to pass.

questions.stem: Metal rods P, Q and R are heated at one end in the same way. The pins on the rods are stuck on with wax and fall off when the wax melts. Which rod is the best conductor of heat?

explain.why: Only one pin fell from Q, so heat travelled slowly in it.
The pins fell off at different times, so they are different.
No pin fell from R, so heat travelled the slowest in it.

solution: All the pins fell from P, so heat travelled furthest and fastest in P.

explain.why: Only A is the poorest, because no pin fell from it.
Two pins fell from B, so heat travelled quite far in it.
All pins fell from C, so it is the best conductor.

solution: No pin fell from A, so heat travelled the slowest in it.

explain.why: D took a long time, so it is a poor conductor.
B took a long time, so it is a poor conductor.
B and D took the longest time, so they are poor conductors.

solution: A shorter time means a better conductor of heat. A and C have the shortest times.

questions.stem: A cup has two plastic walls with a layer of air trapped between them. Why does this help to keep a hot drink hot?
options: Air is a good conductor, so it keeps the heat in
Air is heavy, so it keeps the cup steady
Air makes more heat for the drink
Air is a poor conductor, so heat escapes slowly

explain.why: Air is a poor conductor of heat.
This has nothing to do with heat.
Air does not make heat.

solution: Trapped air is a poor conductor, so it slows the heat loss.

questions.stem: Which material is the best choice for the handle of a frying pan?

explain.why: Aluminium is a good conductor, so the handle would get very hot.
Iron is a good conductor, so the handle would get very hot.
Copper is a good conductor, so the handle would get very hot.

solution: Wood is a poor conductor, so the handle stays cooler.

questions.stem: A wet cloth is hung in the Sun and becomes dry. What happens to the water in the cloth?
options: It loses heat and freezes into ice

explain.why: Condensation happens when a gas loses heat.
The Sun gives heat. The water does not lose heat.
Melting is a solid becoming a liquid.

solution: The water gains heat from the Sun and changes into water vapour.

questions.stem: A metal spoon and a plastic spoon are placed in a bowl of hot soup. After a minute, which end of each spoon feels hotter?
options: The top end of the metal spoon
The top end of the plastic spoon

explain.why: Metal conducts heat much better than plastic.
Metal conducts heat up the spoon to our hand.
Plastic is a poor conductor, so its top end stays cooler.

solution: Heat travels up the metal spoon quickly because metal is a good conductor.

questions.stem: Which sentence about conductors of heat is correct?
options: Rubber is a good conductor of heat
Metals are good conductors of heat
Air is a good conductor of heat
Wood is a good conductor of heat

explain.why: Rubber is a poor conductor.
Air is a poor conductor.
Wood is a poor conductor.

solution: Metals are good conductors; wood, air and rubber are poor conductors.

questions.stem: Overhead cables hang lower on a hot day than on a cold day. Why?
options: The pull of gravity is stronger on a hot day
The poles become shorter on a hot day
The cables contract on a hot day
The cables expand and become longer

explain.why: Gravity does not change with the weather.
Poles also expand when hot, they do not shrink.
Cables expand when they gain heat.

solution: The cables gain heat and expand, so they sag.

questions.stem: An ice cube melts faster on a metal tray than on a plastic tray in the same room. Why?
options: Metal is a poor conductor, so it traps heat
Metal passes heat to the ice faster
Plastic is a good conductor of heat

explain.why: Metal does not make heat.
Metal is a good conductor of heat.
Plastic is a poor conductor.

solution: Metal is a better conductor, so heat reaches the ice faster.

questions.stem: A flask full of coloured water is placed in a bath of hot water. The liquid rises in the thin tube as shown. Why?
options: Air from the bath enters the flask
The water in the flask contracts
The water in the flask becomes heavier
The water in the flask expands

explain.why: The flask is closed. The liquid itself changes.
A liquid contracts when it loses heat.
Heating does not add mass.

solution: The water gains heat, expands and has to rise up the tube.

options: A liquid contracts when it loses heat
A liquid does not change when it loses heat
A liquid expands when it loses heat
A liquid expands when it gains heat

explain.why: The level changed, so the liquid changed.
The level went down, so the liquid took up less space.
The liquid was cooled, not heated, in this test.

solution: The level fell because the cooled liquid contracted.

options: Hot water enters the flask and pushes up the balloon
The air in the flask gains mass
The air in the flask gains heat and expands
The air in the flask contracts

explain.why: The water stays outside the flask.
No air is added, so the mass stays the same.
Air contracts only when it loses heat.

solution: The warmed air expands and fills the balloon.

options: The air in the flask gains heat and expands
The air in the flask loses heat and contracts
The air in the flask turns into a liquid
The ice water enters the balloon

explain.why: The ice water takes heat away from the air.
Air does not turn into a liquid in ice water.
The water stays outside the flask.

solution: Cooled air contracts, so the balloon shrinks.

questions.stem: A metal ball can only just pass through a metal ring when both are at room temperature. Which of the following will stop the ball from passing through?
options: Leaving both in the room for a while

explain.why: Nothing changes, so the ball still passes.
The ring expands, so its hole is bigger.
The ball contracts and is smaller.

solution: Only a bigger ball will not fit. Heating the ball makes it expand.

questions.stem: The table shows the time for the last pin to fall off each rod heated in the same way. Which rod is the best conductor of heat?
options: P, Q and R are equally good

explain.why: Q took longer than P.
R took the longest, so it is the poorest conductor.
The times are different.

The metal spoon gives heat to our hand
The wooden spoon makes more heat than the metal spoon

Our hand is warmer, so heat moves from the hand to the spoon.
Wood does not make heat.

solution: Heat leaves the hand faster through metal, so the metal feels colder.

solution: The water stayed hottest in the wool, so wool is the best insulator.

options: The water contracts and the level drops
The water expands and may crack the bottle

explain.why: The Sun gives heat. Ice forms only when water loses heat.
Heated water expands.
The water gains heat and expands.

solution: Water gains heat and expands. With no room, it pushes on the bottle.

questions.stem: A sealed empty plastic bottle contains only air. It is put in a freezer for an hour. What will happen to the bottle?
options: It will burst because the air turns into ice
It will be a little squashed as the air contracts
It will swell up because the air inside expands
It will stay exactly the same as before

explain.why: Air does not turn into ice in a freezer.
Air contracts when it loses heat.
The cooled air takes up less space.

solution: Cooled air contracts, so the outside air pushes the bottle in.

questions.stem: A table tennis ball has a small dent. When it is put in hot water, the dent pops out. Why?
options: The air inside the ball loses heat and contracts
The plastic of the ball melts and fills the dent
The hot water goes into the ball and pushes out the dent
The air inside the ball gains heat and expands

explain.why: Hot water gives heat to the air.
The plastic does not melt in hot water.
The ball is sealed, so no water enters.

solution: The warmed air expands and pushes the dent out.

questions.stem: Which row shows what happens to a solid, a liquid and a gas when each gains heat?
options: Solid contracts, liquid expands, gas expands
Solid expands, liquid expands, gas expands
Solid expands, liquid contracts, gas expands
Solid expands, liquid expands, gas contracts

explain.why: A solid also expands when heated.
A liquid also expands when heated.
A gas also expands when heated.

solution: Solids, liquids and gases all expand when they gain heat.

questions.stem: A dentist chooses a filling that expands and contracts by about the same amount as a tooth when hot or cold drinks are taken. Why is this important?
options: So that it does not become loose or crack the tooth
So that the filling is heavier than the tooth
So that the filling never gains heat
So that the filling always gets hotter than the tooth does

explain.why: Mass is not the reason.
The filling still gains and loses heat.
That would not help.

solution: Matching expansion keeps the filling snug in the tooth.

questions.stem: A metal bench and a wooden bench in a park have been in the Sun for hours and are both at the same temperature. The metal bench feels hotter to the touch. Why?
options: Metal passes heat to our hand faster
The metal bench is at a higher temperature
Metal makes more heat than wood
Wood is a better conductor than metal

explain.why: They are at the same temperature.
Neither material makes heat.
Metal is the better conductor.

solution: Heat moves from the metal into the hand faster.

Rubber is a poor conductor.

To let the metal expand when it gets hot
To let the metal melt on hot days

The rod contracts when it gains heat

The rod became longer, so it expanded.

solution: The length increased when the rod was heated.

R's temperature rose faster.

options: The same cloth with ice cubes left for different times
One ice cube of the same size in each cloth, in the same room, for equal time
One ice cube in each cloth, each kept in a different room for the same time
Ice cubes of different sizes in each cloth, left in the same room for the same time

explain.why: This tests time, not the cloth.
The room temperature must be the same.
The size of the ice cube also changes the result.

solution: Only the cloth should change.

Heat does not flow along the rod
From point B towards both A and C
From point A towards point C

The temperatures differ, so heat flows.
B is cooler than A, so heat flows into B from A.

solution: Heat flows from the hottest point A to the coolest point C.

So that the liquid does not expand when it is heated

questions.stem: Two metal blocks are in contact as shown. Block A is at 80 °C and block B is at 20 °C. Which statement is correct?
options: Heat flows from A to B until A is at 0 °C
Heat flows from A to B until they are at the same temperature
Heat flows from B to A until they are at the same temperature
Coldness flows from B to A

explain.why: Flow stops when both have the same temperature.
Heat flows from the hotter block.
Heat flows. There is no flow of cold.

solution: Heat flows from the hotter object to the colder one until they are equal.

questions.stem: A cook runs hot water over only the metal lid of a glass jar for a short time. The tight lid then comes off easily. Why?
options: The glass jar contracts but the lid stays the same
The metal lid gains heat and expands
The hot water melts the edge of the lid
The metal lid loses heat and contracts

explain.why: The jar is not the part that was heated.
Hot tap water cannot melt metal.
Hot water gives heat to the lid. It does not take heat away.

solution: The lid expands, so it is no longer gripping the jar tightly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a result of heat gain?
options: Wet clothes drying in the Sun
Butter melting in a hot pan
Water freezing in a freezer tray

explain.why: Evaporation happens when water gains heat.
Melting happens when a solid gains heat.
This is expansion, a result of gaining heat.

solution: Freezing happens when water loses heat.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about heat and conductors are correct?
A: Heat flows from a hot object to a cold object.
B: Air trapped in a jacket slows down heat loss.
C: Plastic conducts heat better than steel.
D: A wooden spoon in hot soup stays cool at the top end for longer than a steel spoon.

explain.why: C is wrong, and A is correct.
C is wrong, and B is correct.
C is wrong because steel is the better conductor.

solution: Plastic is a poorer conductor than steel, so C is wrong.

questions.stem: A student heats a metal rod and measures its length. The table shows the results. Which conclusion is supported?
options: The length of the rod does not depend on temperature
The rod becomes longer only above 100 °C
The hotter the rod, the longer it becomes
The hotter the rod, the shorter it becomes

explain.why: The length changed as the temperature changed.
The rod was already longer at 40 °C than at 20 °C.
The length increased as the temperature rose.

solution: The length rises as the temperature rises.

questions.stem: Why are the fins of some heaters made of metal while the knobs are made of plastic?
options: Both materials conduct heat equally well
Metal gives out heat while plastic keeps the knob cool
Plastic makes heat for the knob
Metal keeps heat in the heater, while plastic gives out heat

explain.why: Metals are good conductors and plastics are poor conductors.
Plastic does not make heat.
Metal conducts heat out, and plastic does not.

solution: Good conductor for heating the room, poor conductor so that the knob is safe to hold.

questions.stem: Wet sand is heated until it is dry. Which change is a result of the sand gaining heat?
options: The water in the sand freezes
The water vapour changes into sand

explain.why: Sand does not change into water.
Freezing happens when water loses heat.
This is not possible.

solution: The water gains heat and evaporates, leaving dry sand.

questions.stem: Four cups each hold 100 g of hot water at 90 °C. Each cup is made of a different material. The table shows the temperature of the water after 15 minutes. Which two cups are most likely made of the poorest conductors of heat?

explain.why: P and Q lost the most heat, so they are good conductors.
Q lost a lot of heat.
P lost a lot of heat.

solution: Cups R and S kept the water hottest.

questions.stem: Concrete slabs on a long road have narrow gaps filled with soft tar. What would happen on a very hot day if there were no gaps?
options: The slabs would contract and pull apart from one another
The slabs would expand and crack
The slabs would melt and flow away from the road

explain.why: Expansion would have no room.
Slabs expand on a hot day.
The concrete does not melt in the heat.

solution: Without gaps, the expanding slabs press against each other.

questions.stem: A student holds an iron rod with one end in a flame. Soon the end near his hand becomes hot. He then holds a wooden stick the same way and the end near his hand stays cool. What can he conclude?
options: Iron makes more heat than wood
Wood is a good insulator because it gives out cold
Wood conducts heat better than iron
Iron conducts heat better than wood

explain.why: Neither makes heat. The flame supplies it.
Wood does not give out cold. It conducts poorly.
Heat reached his hand faster through the iron.

solution: Heat reached the far end of the iron but not the wood.

questions.stem: A ball just passes through a ring at 20 °C. The ball is heated to 80 °C and placed on the ring. It does not pass. After a few minutes it passes through again. What most likely happened?
options: The ball gained more heat and expanded further
The ring contracted so that its hole became bigger
The ball cooled down and contracted

explain.why: A bigger ball would not pass.
Mass does not change with temperature.
A contracting ring has a smaller hole.

solution: As the ball cooled it contracted until it fitted the ring.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be best for making a container to keep ice cream cold for a long time?
options: A box with thick foam walls
A box made of aluminium foil

explain.why: Glass lets heat in quite easily when thin.
Steel is a good conductor, so heat would flow in quickly.
Aluminium is a good conductor.

solution: Plastic foam traps air, a poor conductor, so heat gets in slowly.

questions.stem: A rubber hot-water bottle and a metal can hold water at the same temperature. Why does the metal can feel hotter to the touch?
options: The water in the can is at a higher temperature
Rubber conducts heat better than metal does
Rubber gives out cold to the hand
Metal conducts heat to the hand faster than rubber does

explain.why: Both hold water at the same temperature.
Metal is the better conductor.
Rubber does not give out cold.

solution: Heat reaches the hand faster through metal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of heat?

explain.why: Cold milk is not a source of heat.
A cold spoon does not give out heat.
Ice is cold. It takes in heat.

solution: The Sun gives out a lot of heat.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives out heat when electricity flows through it?

explain.why: A rubber ball does not give out heat.
A wooden spoon does not give out heat.
Water does not give out heat when electricity is not used on it.

solution: A toaster changes electrical energy into heat.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?

explain.why: A ruler measures length.
A measuring cylinder measures volume.
A balance measures mass.

solution: Temperature is measured with a thermometer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the unit used to measure temperature?

explain.why: Newton is a unit of force.
Centimetre is a unit of length.
Gram is a unit of mass.

solution: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

questions.stem: Temperature is a measure of how ____ an object is.

explain.why: Mass tells us how heavy an object is.
Size is not temperature.
Speed is not temperature.

solution: Temperature tells how hot or cold something is.

questions.stem: Heat is a form of ____.

explain.why: Heat has no mass and takes up no space.
Heat is not a push or a pull.
Heat is not a material.

solution: Heat is a form of energy.

questions.stem: A cup of hot tea is left on a table in a cool room. Which way does heat flow?
options: From the table to the tea
From the tea to the surroundings
From the surroundings to the tea

explain.why: The tea is hotter than the table.
Heat flows from hot to cold.
There is a difference in temperature, so heat flows.

solution: Heat flows from the hotter tea to the cooler surroundings.

questions.stem: Ali puts a thermometer into a cup of water. What is the reading on the thermometer?

explain.why: The liquid is below the 26 mark.
Count the small marks again from 20.
The liquid is above the 20 mark.

solution: The liquid is two small marks above 20, so it reads 24 °C.

questions.stem: Mei puts her left hand into hot water and her right hand into cold water for a minute. She then puts both hands into warm water. How do her hands feel?
options: The left hand feels hotter than the right hand
The left hand feels cooler than the right hand
Neither hand can feel the water

explain.why: The left hand was in hotter water, so the warm water feels cooler to it.
Both hands can feel it.
Our hands judge by the heat gained or lost.

solution: Our hands are poor judges of temperature, so we use a thermometer.

questions.stem: Why do we use a thermometer instead of our hand to find how hot water is?
options: Our sense of hot and cold is not exact
Our hand is always colder than the water
Water cannot be felt with the hand
A thermometer makes the water hotter

explain.why: This is not always true.
We can feel water. We just cannot measure exactly.
A thermometer does not change the water.

solution: A thermometer gives an exact reading.

questions.stem: Which list contains only sources of heat?
options: The Sun, burning wood, an electric stove
Burning wood, a refrigerator shelf, the Sun
The Sun, ice, an electric stove
An electric stove, a snowman, burning wood

explain.why: A refrigerator shelf is not a source of heat.
Ice is not a source of heat.
A snowman is not a source of heat.

solution: The Sun, burning wood and electric stoves all give out heat.

questions.stem: Why do our hands become warm when we rub them together?
options: Heat flows from the cold air to our hands
Our hands take in cold from the air

explain.why: Heat flows from hot to cold.
Cold is not taken in.
Mass is not related to heat here.

solution: Rubbing makes friction, which makes heat.

questions.stem: A hot metal ball is put into cold water. The graph shows the temperatures of the ball and the water. Which line is for the ball?

explain.why: The ball is the hot object. It starts at 100 °C.
The two lines start at different temperatures.
One of the lines belongs to the ball.

solution: The ball was hotter at the start, so its line starts higher.
